_status: DRAFT, NOT IMPORTED. First municipal-level slice in the AF branch (G.13) -- pivots down from the federal-level CPI/pension work of G.1-G.12 to city/state government finance. Sitting in src/data/research/ pending Thomas's review.
_note: The strongest finding is a genuine but DISCRETIONARY inflation-indexation clause in Lagos's own Land Use Charge Law, 2018 (Section 10(2)): valuation rates 'may be set to rise in line with the rate of inflation as may be determined by the Commissioner' between mandatory five-year reviews -- real, but it names no specific CPI source and leaves the determination to ministerial discretion, so no edge was drawn to a CPI report. Lagos's own MTEF and Citizens' Budget are genuine, fetchable primary documents that name NBS's CPI rebasing in their forecasting narrative and show clear dependence on FAAC/Federation Account transfers. The federal Allocation of Revenue Act sets the vertical 56/24/20 split but was searched in full and does not name Lagos specifically; NBS's own monthly FAAC Disbursement Report does name Lagos with actual disbursement figures, which is the stronger and more concrete link used here. No primary source was found for CPI-linked LAWMA waste tariffs or Lagos Water Corporation tariffs -- recorded as NOT-FOUND rather than inferred.

_open_questions.question: Lagos's own MTEF 2026-2028 (Table 8) sources its National and State inflation forecasts to 'Economic Intelligence Department, LBS' (Lagos Bureau of Statistics), not NBS directly -- distinct from the narrative NBS citation elsewhere in the same document. No specific, citable LBS CPI/inflation report was located or opened this session; worth a dedicated look.

Lagos's own MTEF 2026-2028 contains an internal inconsistency about the NBS CPI rebasing: para 41 states 'rebasing... in January 2025... base year updated from 2009 to 2024,' while another passage in the same document states 'rebasing... in April 2025 -- with 2019 as the new base year.' Flagged, not resolved -- an error in Lagos's own document, not something a researcher can adjudicate.

reports.title: Land Use Charge Law of Lagos State, 2018
reports.publisher: Lagos State House of Assembly / Lagos State Government
reports.description: Lagos State's consolidated property-tax statute, replacing the 2001 Land Use Charge Law. Sets the LUC formula (Land Value + Building Development Value) x Relief Rate x Charge Rate, and directs that "the land value rates and building value rates may be set to rise in line with the rate of inflation as may be determined by the Commissioner" between the mandatory five-year valuation reviews. Discretionary, not a named-source formula.

reports.title: Lagos State Government Medium Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF) 2026–2028
reports.publisher: Lagos State Ministry of Economic Planning and Budget (MEPB), Economic Intelligence Department
reports.description: Lagos State's medium-term fiscal planning document underpinning the Y2026 budget. Its macroeconomic framework (Table 8) sets three-year National and State CPI/inflation assumptions, and its revenue narrative discusses NBS's January 2025 CPI rebasing as providing "a firmer foundation for policy targeting and fiscal forecasting particularly relevant for Lagos." Revenue charts for Statutory Allocation, mineral revenues, CIT and VAT are sourced to "Monthly FAAC Allocation" data.
reports.cadence_note: Prepared annually ahead of the state budget cycle; the document itself shows some inconsistent leftover references to prior-year MTEF cycles.

reports.title: Lagos State Government Y2026 Citizens' Budget (Budget of Shared Prosperity)
reports.publisher: Lagos State Ministry of Economic Planning and Budget (MEPB)
reports.description: The public-facing simplified version of Lagos State's approved Y2026 budget. States that N909bn of budget revenue "will come from the Federation Account," comprising VAT, Statutory Allocation and other FAAC receipts, and defines "Statutory Allocation" as "a transfer from the Federal Allocation Accounts Committee (FAAC)."

reports.title: Allocation of Revenue (Federation Account, etc.) Act
reports.description: The federal statute prescribing the vertical distribution of the Federation Account: "the Federal Government 56.00 per cent; the State Governments 24.00 per cent; the Local Government Councils 20.00 per cent," and establishing FAAC. Full text searched for "Lagos" -- zero matches. Horizontal (inter-state) shares are allocated only by general factors (equality, population, land mass, social development indices), never listing individual states.
reports.cadence_note: Original Act commenced 22 January 1982; amended 1992 No.106 and by S.I. 9 of 2002 as printed in the retrieved text.

reports.title: Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) Disbursement Report
reports.publisher: National Bureau of Statistics (NBS), data sourced from the Office of the Accountant General of the Federation (OAGF)
reports.description: NBS's recurring monthly report of actual Federation Account disbursements to Federal, State and Local Governments, broken out by individual state. The February 2024 Disbursement report lists Lagos State's gross statutory-type allocation as ₦35,885,123,715.62 and net as ₦23,624,839,736.46 -- naming Lagos specifically, unlike the enabling Act.

dependencies.basis: MTEF: "the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) implemented a long-overdue rebasing of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) in January 2025... This methodological upgrade enhances the quality of price statistics and provides a firmer foundation for policy targeting and fiscal forecasting particularly relevant for Lagos." The MTEF explicitly names NBS's CPI rebasing as informing its own forecasting narrative, though its own Table 8 inflation figures are separately sourced to Lagos's own LBS, not NBS directly.

MTEF Figure 17 ('FAAC Statutory Allocation Budget vs Actual: 2019-2025') and related charts are captioned 'Source: Monthly FAAC Allocation,' and the MTEF's revenue-trend analysis 'looks at Statutory Allocation, VAT, IGR, other Federation Account receipts... for the period 2018-2024... and a three (3) year forecast.'

Citizens Budget: "The Total sum of N909bn will come from the Federation Account... N116bn from Statutory Allocation, and N119bn from other FAAC receipts," and its glossary defines Statutory Allocation as "a transfer from the Federal Allocation Accounts Committee (FAAC)... shared between the three tiers of government using sharing ratios." Weaker basis than the MTEF edge above since this document carries no explicit 'Source:' line.
